identity.title: C-SDLC bind topology scan misresolves historical worktree dot records

values.summary: Freeze canonical topology semantics, classify relevance from cheap metadata, verify only relevant records, add issue/path diagnostics, prove the #5791-shaped success and genuine collision failures, then run focused review and publication.

steps.action: Approve the source-grounded canonical topology and relevance-ordering design.
Implement canonical-root relevance classification and contextual filesystem errors in lifecycle.rs.
Add focused real-binary success and genuine-collision regression cases in gate2.rs.
Run focused validation, resolve exact-head review, publish a closing PR, shepherd it green, and finish through typed authority.

invariants: Requested issue and true topology owners are always fully verified
Relative worktree paths never inherit an arbitrary scan root
Unrelated retained records cannot become authored-artifact dependencies
risks: Choosing the wrong canonical root could hide a genuine relative-worktree owner
Filtering before verification could accidentally skip a corrupt relevant record
Context wrapping could erase the original typed error category
Fixture setup could prove only a helper rather than the real bind binary
stop_conditions: The classifier cannot prove irrelevance before full verification
A genuine issue, branch, or canonical-worktree collision stops failing closed
Correctness would require mutating retained historical evidence
Scope expands beyond bind topology classification and focused proof
